head: fe595a4d67aac199a98551eb471cdcac2622510a
scope: KdsOrder contract integrity + transition whitelist + recall/undo semantics

findings.title: Recall mechanism is browser-local localStorage with NO backend round-trip and NO audit trail

evidence.code_excerpt: bumpItem ({ commit, state }, { orderId, itemId }) { ... persistMap(next); }, recallItem({ commit, state }, { orderId, itemId, now = Date.now() }) { ... persistMap(next); return { ok: true }; }
evidence.cross_ref_no_backend_route: routes/api.php:1005-1011 declares ONLY index/changeStatus/items/sync — no /kds-order/bump and no /kds-order/recall endpoints

impact: Cross-browser inconsistency: chef A bumps item, chef B (same station, different tab) cannot see bump state
Cache-clear or private browsing wipes ALL bump/recall history mid-shift
No NF525 audit_log entry for bump events — fiscal auditors cannot trace plate-readiness timeline
No backend authoritative source-of-truth for KDS line-level workflow — frontend is sole arbiter
Owner-expected 60s recall grace (kds_recall_grace_expired i18n label) enforced by Date.now() only — clock skew across stations not validated
findings.contract_intent_gap: Naming kds_recall + i18n key fr.json:1176 'délai d'annulation 60 s' suggests an order-status recall (PREPARED → PREPARING transition). Actual implementation is per-item bump-undo within ONE browser session. Owner-facing semantics likely diverge from implementation.
findings.scope_minimal_heal_recommendation: Add backend endpoint POST /kds-order/{order}/items/{item}/bump and POST /kds-order/{order}/items/{item}/recall persisting to a new kds_item_events append-only table; broadcast via existing OrderStatusChanged-pattern Echo channel; reconcile localStorage as a write-through cache. Estimated 4-6h.

findings.title: Transition whitelist forbids backward jumps (PREPARED → PREPARING) — recall cannot restore order to PREPARING via Order.status

evidence.code_excerpt: public static function canTransition(int $from, int $to): bool { if ($from === $to) { return self::isVisibleStatus($from); } return ($from === OrderStatus::ACCEPT && $to === OrderStatus::PREPARING) || ($from === OrderStatus::PREPARING && $to === OrderStatus::PREPARED); }
evidence.cross_ref: app/Http/Requests/Kds/KdsOrderStatusRequest.php:34-41 rules require Rule::in([ACCEPT, PREPARING, PREPARED]); FormRequest authz restricted to Admin/Branch Manager/Chef/POS Operator/Cashier

impact: If owner intent is order-level recall (PREPARED → PREPARING for plate rework), current backend forbids it and would 422 invalid_status_transition
Forward-only state machine intersects with localStorage-only bump/recall in a confusing way: a chef can 'recall' an item visually but the Order.status stays PREPARED if all items had been bumped
No re-entrant transition allowed even for genuine error correction (e.g. wrong order marked PREPARED)
findings.scope_minimal_heal_recommendation: Document explicitly that backward transitions are forbidden by design (NF525 audit chain immutability principle); add a separate kds.order_correction endpoint guarded by Branch Manager+ role that emits a void/replay audit_log entry rather than mutating Order.status. Estimated 6-8h with sentinel test.

findings.title: KDS bump state stored under same localStorage key for ALL operators on a shared station
findings.impact: Station shared between Chef A morning shift and Chef B afternoon shift carries A's stale bump state into B's session unless explicitly cleared. No user_id namespace.
findings.scope_minimal_heal_recommendation: Salt the localStorage key with auth user_id and/or branch_id, e.g. STORAGE_BUMPED = `kds.bumped_items_v1.${userId}.${branchId}`. Estimated 1h with vitest.

findings.title: Order.status mutation in changeStatus() executes without idempotency-key check

evidence.comparison: IdempotencyKeyMiddleware (CLAUDE.md §9) is applied to POST mutating endpoints elsewhere but NOT to KDS change-status

findings.impact: Network retry on flaky wifi can double-dispatch SendOrderMail/Sms/Push and emit a second OrderStatusChanged event. The expected_status optimistic lock catches the 2nd attempt (returns 409) but only AFTER mail/sms have been dispatched on the first attempt — race remains between transaction commit and listener side-effects on retry.
findings.scope_minimal_heal_recommendation: Wrap changeStatus route with IdempotencyKeyMiddleware similar to other mutating POSTs. Estimated 1h.
findings.audit_status: Read-verified — middleware absence confirmed by grep on routes/api.php

findings.title: KdsSyncService::computeOrderVersion documented TODO not yet implemented (per-order version stamp)

evidence.code_excerpt: TODO(F-03 / Phase 3 dette technique D-03bis): when the planned `status_changed_at` column lands on Order, switch to `max(updated_at_unix, status_changed_at_unix)` to avoid skipping cards whose status moved without other field updates.

findings.impact: Edge case: if an order's only mutation is status flip and no other updated_at change, version compared against client may equal — frontend version-gate may skip the render update.
findings.scope_minimal_heal_recommendation: Add status_changed_at TIMESTAMP migration on orders + use max(updated_at, status_changed_at) for version. Estimated 3h.
findings.audit_status: Read-verified — TODO comment present at line 152

verification_pattern_check.recall_idempotency_test_missing: tests/Feature/Kds/KdsRecallIdempotencyTest.php — NOT FOUND (would be moot since recall is frontend-only)

summary_one_line: Recall + bump are pure localStorage frontend-state with no backend persistence/audit, transition whitelist is forward-only (correct for NF525) but contract intent for 'recall' diverges from implementation; 16 KDS tests cover backend slice exhaustively.
